utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. This is now a public session. You can begin, Mr. Greaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Witness DB, would you tell us, please, what your ethnic background is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: How long have you known Goran Jelisic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I've known Goran, as I'm older than him, since childhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: By how much are you older than Goran?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About ten years, thereabouts. Ten or eleven.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Initially, were you just acquaintances who would exchange greetings when you met in town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you became close friends?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was when Goran grew up and started going out with his friends in town.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Amongst the people who were in his group of friends, were you the only Muslim, or were there other Muslims as members of that group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there were all sorts. There were Muslims and Croats and Serbs and Romanies, Gypsies.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did Goran Jelisic, in your presence, ever demonstrate a hostility towards members of other races or any sort of nationalist ideas towards other races?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: In April 1992, I think that fighting broke out in your home town of Bijeljina. Did you see Goran after that fighting had taken place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: When did you next see Goran after the fighting in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly, but it was perhaps some three months later, thereabouts, sometime in July or August. In the summer, at any rate.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And when you saw him, had his attitude changed towards you as a Muslim in any way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did he offer any sort of assistance to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He offered me assistance. The refugees had already started, so that I would not have any problems with the refugees; that is to say, with them evicting me from my own home. And he said if I needed any help along those lines that I could contact him and he would help me as far as he was able.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Later on in 1992, did you continue to see Goran?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not as much, because I was busy. I was amongst the fighting ranks in the Posavina front region, so we didn't communicate, and saw each other less frequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: When you returned from the military activities, did you see him again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him, but we didn't go around together, because Goran lived in town, and I went about my own business, so we didn't actually go around together after the fighting activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Yes. Would you wait there, please, Witness DB.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Nice?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Only a couple of questions of this witness, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Just yes or no: Were you spoken to by the investigator, Mr. Berberovic, on behalf of the Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Then who on behalf of the Defence did you speak to or did you give a statement to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A lawyer, Veselin Londrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Has it ever been your recollection -- no, I'll start again. You say that the only occasion when you met Jelisic was in July or August of 1992; that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And it has never been your case -- I'm so sorry. It has never been your case, it's never been your recollection, that you met him as early as April or May of 1992, has it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: At the time he gave you assistance, or offered you some kind of assistance, did he reveal to you that he knew he was already a wanted man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: At the time he allegedly offered you assistance, he appeared to have some influence with the local authorities and was able to move around freely; would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: One other topic, very shortly: You knew him before 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did you know him in 1989?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did you see him regularly then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not really regularly, but whenever we would see each other, we would have a drink and have a talk, a chat. But this was never anything to do with politics.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: So you got to know of his getting involved in criminal offences?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: He never told you about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You didn't know of his drug addiction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You see, Jelisic has told others that the root of all his problems happened in January 1989, when his wife's father came to his house, and since then, he took the road to criminal activity. He never discussed that with you, did he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And indeed, he kept all his criminal activity from you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: No re-examination, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Judge Riad, do you have any questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Witness DB, good morning. You said that you knew the accused since his childhood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: What did you know about his family life, about the way he was brought up? In short.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was from a fine family, and I couldn't believe that he could do anything of the kind for which he stands accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: No, I wanted to know, was he brought up by his parents? Was he a lonely child? Was he left unattended to? Who brought him up, and when did he leave his home? If you knew him since his childhood, you could give us some information.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His family is a fine one, as I said, and if he took the wrong road as a young man, before the war --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the wrong road, and when was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, like any young man who likes to get his kicks from cafes, stays out late at night --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I don't want any young man; I want Jelisic. If you have nothing to say, please save us the trouble. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Judge Riad. Judge Rodrigues, no questions? I have no questions either. Thank you, Witness DB. Your testimony is now concluded. Please do not move. I think that we are not yet ready for the video conference, according to what the registrar has told us.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct. I reconfirm it will be around 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Very well. That will allow us to take a nice break that the interpreters have actually, in fact, deserved, in advance. We will break until around 11.00, when the registrar calls us to tell us that the video conference is ready. Court is adjourned.
